origins: In long illness, prayers can feel unanswered and God silent. Loneliness and pain make His presence hard to sense.
teaches: “Why, O LORD, do You stand far off?” the psalmist asks. And yet: “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted.” “When you pass through the waters, I will be with you.” Hebrews records God’s promise, “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you” (Hebrews 13:5). Feelings of abandonment are real, and they are not the final word. Even Jesus on the cross cried out, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” (Psalm 22:1). God understands the sense of abandonment, and He has not left you.
self_statements: He is silent because He is gone.
errors: Believing God is either felt or absent.
Predicting that God will never come near.
Feeling alone and concluding that God is gone.
questions: When have I felt God near before?
Who has shown up for me in this illness?
What does Scripture promise about God’s presence in hardship?
What did the psalmists do with feelings of abandonment?
How might God be present in ways I do not feel?
What small act of trust could I take?
truth: Feeling abandoned is not the same as being abandoned. God promises to be with me through the waters. I can cry out honestly, look for His presence in people and Scripture, and trust Him.
hw_truths: God is with me through the waters.
He is near to the brokenhearted.
log: Each week, note one sign of God’s presence or care.
prayer: Lord, I feel abandoned. Draw near, hold my hand, and let me know You are here. Amen.
